process.lead: The pipeline I run every day on my own platform — and set up for teams.

steps.name: Orchestrator
steps.text: A planner splits the task into steps. A stronger model plans and cheaper ones execute — Opus plans, Sonnet works — then the results reconverge.

steps.name: Agents
steps.text: Sub-agents with roles — planner, coder, tester, reviewer — each with its own tools and token budget. Every run gets its own Docker sandbox and git worktree.

steps.name: Checks & evals
steps.text: An agent may push only after typecheck, linters and tests pass. An eval harness runs the same tasks in two setups and compares pass rate, attempts and cost.

steps.name: Production
steps.text: I review the diff and own the release: deploys with a health check and automatic rollback, and no public attack surface.

principles.name: NDA-safe by default
principles.text: Data is anonymized before it reaches any AI tool.

principles.name: Cost is engineering too
principles.text: A local code graph made agent recon 13.6× cheaper.

principles.name: Proof over promises
principles.text: The first agent-authored PR is merged to main; a real multi-agent task finished with 24 of 24 tests green.

items.a: I work with Claude Code and my own agents every day: agents plan, write and test, while I set the task, review every diff and own what ships. Nothing merges until typecheck, linters and tests pass.

items.q: Are you an AI engineer or a full-stack developer?
items.a: Both, in practice. I build LLM features and AI agents, and I've shipped React, Vue and Node.js products for {years} years. AI is how I work; a working product is what I deliver.

items.q: Can you bring AI into our development team under an NDA?
items.a: Yes — I did it at Mercury Properties: lectures and hands-on sessions, then editor plugins, custom MCP servers and a RAG index over the code and docs. Data is anonymized before it reaches any AI tool, so client and business information never leaves in identifiable form. Emergency hotfixes dropped 4× in two months.

items.q: Which models and tools do you work with?
items.a: Claude through the Anthropic API and Claude Code, OpenAI models behind LiteLLM routing, MCP for tools, RAG and a local code graph for context. The model is a runtime choice, not an architectural commitment.

items.q: How do you price a project?
items.a: A fixed price for an agreed result, settled before work starts. If you'd like to see how I work first, start with a test week.

items.q: Do you work remotely? Where are you based?
items.a: I'm based in {city}, {country} ({utc}). I spent three years fully remote in a US team at POWR.io across a 12-hour time difference, so remote and async work is routine for me.
